60935.recognize_zh: 大細胞的核呈摺疊、腎形不規則，染色質比嗜中性球細緻，外圍大量灰藍色細胞質帶有細小嗜天青顆粒與多個空泡，細胞邊緣不規則，是典型的單核球（monocyte）。
features: Large cell, roughly twice the diameter of adjacent red cells, with an irregular, angular cytoplasmic outline
Folded, indented/kidney-shaped nucleus with moderately condensed but lacy chromatin and no nucleoli
Abundant grey-blue cytoplasm with fine, dust-like azurophilic granules
Multiple small cytoplasmic vacuoles, clustered near the nuclear indentation and at the periphery
Background normochromic red cells and a single small platelet
60935.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at high magnification shows a large mononuclear cell surrounded by normochromic red cells. The cell has a folded, kidney-shaped nucleus with lacy, moderately condensed chromatin, no visible nucleoli, and abundant grey-blue cytoplasm containing fine azurophilic granules and multiple small vacuoles. The cytoplasmic border is irregular. Findings are consistent with a normal mature monocyte.

ddx.vs: Promonocytes have finer open chromatin, often a nucleolus and delicately folded nuclei, and are counted as blast equivalents.
Reactive lymphocytes have a rounder nucleus with denser chromatin and cytoplasm with peripheral basophilia that hugs adjacent red cells, without fine granules and vacuoles.
Neutrophilic precursors have pink cytoplasm with specific granules and more coarsely clumped chromatin rather than grey-blue vacuolated cytoplasm.

60295.recognize_zh: 密集的紅血球中散在數顆體積較大、染成藍灰紫色、缺乏中央淡染區的多染性紅血球（polychromatophilic cells），整體紅血球偏大，符合新生兒血液常見的多染性（polychromasia）。
features: Scattered larger red cells with bluish-gray to lilac cytoplasm (polychromatophilic cells)
Polychromatophilic cells lack central pallor and are larger than surrounding red cells
Background red cells relatively large with mild anisocytosis, fitting neonatal red cell indices
Occasional crenated red cells, likely artifact
Scattered platelets; no nucleated red cells or inclusions in this field
60295.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear from a neonate shows a crowded field of relatively large red cells with mild anisocytosis. Numerous scattered polychromatophilic red cells are present, appearing larger and bluish-gray without central pallor, reflecting residual RNA in reticulocytes. Occasional crenated cells are seen and platelets are present. Findings are consistent with polychromasia, which is physiologic in the newborn given the high reticulocyte count, but may be increased further in hemolysis (e.g. hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn).

ddx.vs: Spherocytes are small, dense and orange-pink without central pallor, whereas polychromatophilic cells are large and bluish.
A staining artifact colors all cells similarly, whereas true polychromasia affects individual larger cells that stain with new methylene blue as reticulocytes.
Basophilic stippling shows discrete blue dots within red cells, whereas polychromasia is diffuse blue-gray cytoplasmic tinting.

135.recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片與切片中可見大量具細緻染色質與核仁的芽細胞，並伴隨許多單核／小型發育不良巨核細胞（micromegakaryocytes，CD61類標記凸顯）；染色體核型顯示 -5、-7、-17 與 marker 染色體的複雜單套型核型，NGS 見 TP53 變異，綜合支持 AML-MRC。
features: Bone marrow aspirate dominated by medium-to-large blasts with high N:C ratio, finely dispersed chromatin, visible nucleoli and scant basophilic cytoplasm, some with folded or indented nuclei
Dysplastic megakaryocytes: small mononuclear/hypolobated forms with a single round nucleus and granular cytoplasm (aspirate, H&E, and megakaryocytic IHC)
Hypercellular trephine with sheets of immature cells, open chromatin, prominent nucleoli and mitotic figures, with scattered clustered small megakaryocytes
Megakaryocytic marker IHC highlights numerous small, mono- and bilobated megakaryocytes in loose clusters
Peripheral blood with marked thrombocytopenia, red cell anisopoikilocytosis and an occasional circulating blast
Complex monosomal karyotype (single copies of chromosomes 5, 7, 16 and 17 plus marker chromosomes) and a TP53 single-nucleotide variant on NGS read alignment
135.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked thrombocytopenia, red cell anisopoikilocytosis and a rare circulating blast. The bone marrow aspirate is cellular and largely replaced by blasts with fine chromatin, nucleoli and scant cytoplasm, accompanied by dysplastic mononuclear and hypolobated megakaryocytes; the iron stain shows scattered iron granules without conspicuous ring sideroblasts in the field shown. The trephine biopsy is hypercellular with sheets of blasts and increased mitoses, and megakaryocytic immunostaining highlights numerous small, dysplastic, clustered megakaryocytes; a nuclear immunostain (red chromogen) is strongly positive in a large proportion of cells, a pattern compatible with p53 overexpression. Karyotype shows a complex monosomal karyotype including monosomy 5, 7 and 17 with marker chromosomes, and NGS demonstrates a TP53 variant. Findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia with myelodysplasia-related changes (complex karyotype, TP53-mutated).

ddx.vs: Also shows small hypolobated megakaryocytes, but is defined by the 3q26 rearrangement on karyotype, whereas this case has monosomies 5, 7 and 17 without chromosome 3 abnormality.

ddx.dx: AML with mutated NPM1 with multilineage dysplasia
ddx.vs: Can mimic multilineage dysplasia but typically has a normal karyotype with cup-like blast nuclei; an MDS-related complex karyotype as seen here takes precedence.

Blasts themselves express megakaryocytic markers (CD41/CD61) with cytoplasmic blebs and often marrow fibrosis, whereas here the CD61-type stain marks dysplastic maturing megakaryocytes rather than the blast population.
Morphology and TP53/complex karyotype overlap entirely; separation rests on a history of prior cytotoxic therapy or radiation.

135.stain: Wright-Giemsa, H&E, Prussian blue, IHC; karyotype; NGS
captions: Peripheral blood: marked thrombocytopenia with anisopoikilocytosis and a rare circulating blast (top).
Bone marrow aspirate: sheets of blasts with fine chromatin, nucleoli and folded nuclei (arrows).
Bone marrow aspirate: dysplastic mononuclear megakaryocyte with a single round nucleus (arrow) among blasts.
Bone marrow aspirate: small hypolobated megakaryocytes with granular cytoplasm (arrows) amid blasts.
Trephine biopsy, H&E: hypercellular marrow with sheets of immature cells next to a bony trabecula.
Trephine biopsy, H&E high power: blasts with open chromatin and nucleoli (arrows) and a mitotic figure.
Trephine biopsy, H&E: small mononuclear dysplastic megakaryocyte (arrow).
Aspirate iron stain: scattered iron granules, no conspicuous ring sideroblasts in this field.
Trephine IHC (red chromogen): strong nuclear staining in many cells, compatible with p53 overexpression.
Megakaryocytic marker IHC: numerous small, clustered dysplastic megakaryocytes.
Megakaryocytic marker IHC: mononuclear micromegakaryocyte (arrow) and hypolobated forms.
Megakaryocytic marker IHC high power: bilobed and mononuclear dysplastic megakaryocytes.
Karyotype: complex monosomal karyotype with single chromosomes 5, 7, 16 and 17 (arrows) and marker chromosomes.

71.recognize_zh: 骨髓切片高度細胞化，可見一片片黏聚、胞質嗜鹼性、核仁明顯的大型不成熟細胞（形態像早期紅血球前驅細胞），旁邊混有大量嗜酸性球；周邊血有顆粒異常的嗜酸性球與粗大嗜鹼性顆粒細胞。此形態易被誤判為紅血球白血病，需染色體 t(8;9)(p22;p24) 確認 PCM1-JAK2。
features: Core biopsy: markedly hypercellular marrow (near 100%) with large cohesive sheets and nodules of immature cells at low power
Immature cells are large with round to oval nuclei, open chromatin, distinct nucleoli, moderate amphophilic to basophilic cytoplasm and frequent mitoses, resembling early erythroid precursors
Background of numerous eosinophils and eosinophilic precursors with maturing granulocytes
Peripheral blood: eosinophil with abnormal, sparse and unevenly distributed granules and cytoplasmic vacuoles; large cells with coarse dark basophilic granules and an atypical monocytoid cell

IHC (marker unlabeled): strong membranous staining of the immature cell sheets with a sharp border against negative surrounding marrow; a second marker stains scattered interstitial cells with cytoplasmic granular pattern
71.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an eosinophil with abnormal, sparse and unevenly distributed granules and cytoplasmic vacuoles, as well as large cells with coarse basophilic granules and an atypical monocytoid cell. The bone marrow core biopsy is markedly hypercellular and contains large cohesive sheets and nodules of large immature cells with open chromatin, conspicuous nucleoli, basophilic cytoplasm and frequent mitoses, resembling left-shifted erythroid precursors, set in a background of maturing granulocytes with prominent eosinophilia. Immunohistochemistry (markers not labeled in the figure) shows strong membranous staining of the immature cell sheets, and a second stain highlights scattered interstitial cells; lineage assignment cannot be confirmed from the images alone. Morphology alone could suggest acute erythroid leukemia, but with eosinophilia, splenomegaly and a t(8;9)(p22;p24) translocation, findings are consistent with myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with PCM1-JAK2.

ddx.vs: Pure erythroid leukemia shows sheets of proerythroblasts often with complex karyotype and TP53 mutation, whereas here the erythroid-like sheets occur with eosinophilia and a t(8;9)(p22;p24) PCM1-JAK2 fusion that defines the entity.

ddx.dx: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with PDGFRA, PDGFRB or FGFR1 rearrangement
ddx.vs: These share eosinophilia and MPN-like marrow but lack the characteristic erythroid predominance and are separated by FISH/cytogenetics for the respective rearrangements rather than morphology.
CEL-NOS requires exclusion of PDGFRA/PDGFRB/FGFR1/PCM1-JAK2 rearrangements and does not show sheets of immature erythroid-like cells.
SM shows compact aggregates of spindled or oval mast cells that are CD117+/tryptase+/CD25+ with KIT D816V, rather than sheets of large cells with open chromatin and nucleoli.

captions: Peripheral blood: dysplastic eosinophil with abnormal sparse granules and vacuoles
Peripheral blood: large cells with coarse basophilic granules and an atypical monocytoid cell
Bone marrow biopsy, low power: markedly hypercellular marrow with darker cellular nodules
Bone marrow biopsy: sheets of immature cells adjacent to bony trabeculae
Bone marrow biopsy: cohesive sheet of large immature cells with nucleoli
High power: immature erythroid-like cells with mitoses (left) next to marked eosinophilia (right)
IHC (marker unlabeled): strong membranous staining of immature cell sheets

66247.recognize_zh: 畫面中央是一顆大的巨噬細胞，細胞質豐富、淡藍色帶細纖維狀紋理，邊緣緊貼幾顆核濃縮深染、細胞質灰藍的紅血球前驅細胞（normoblast）；周圍混有各階段顆粒球前驅細胞，呈現正常骨髓中的紅血球生成島（erythroblastic island）。
features: Large central macrophage with abundant pale blue, finely fibrillar cytoplasm and an irregular, partly folded nucleus
Several erythroid precursors abutting the macrophage, with round nuclei, condensed chromatin and gray-blue to polychromatic cytoplasm
Numerous small erythroid precursors (polychromatic and orthochromatic normoblasts) scattered in the background with round, dense nuclei
Admixed granulocytic precursors (promyelocytes, myelocytes, bands) with pink granular cytoplasm showing orderly maturation
No blast excess, megaloblastic change or obvious dysplasia in this field
66247.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (Leishman stain, oil immersion) shows a cellular field with trilineage-appropriate precursors. A large central macrophage with abundant pale blue fibrillar cytoplasm is closely apposed by erythroid precursors showing progressive nuclear condensation and cytoplasmic hemoglobinization, forming an erythroblastic island; the ring of attached erythroblasts is incomplete in this plane of the smear. The surrounding granulocytic precursors mature in an orderly fashion, and no increase in blasts, megaloblastic change or dyserythropoiesis is identified. Findings are consistent with a normal erythroblastic island in bone marrow.

ddx.vs: A hemophagocytic histiocyte contains engulfed intact erythrocytes, nucleated cells or platelets within its cytoplasm, whereas island erythroblasts sit on the macrophage surface without being ingested.
Pseudo-Gaucher and sea-blue histiocytes occur in high-turnover states such as CML or ITP and are defined by the cytoplasmic storage material itself, not by a rosette of attached erythroblasts.
Tumor clumps are cohesive sheets of atypical non-hematopoietic cells with large pleomorphic nuclei, unlike a single benign macrophage surrounded by maturing normoblasts.

61063.recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中央一顆大型組織球，雙核、胞質豐富呈淡灰藍色並有細緻纖維狀紋理，類似皺摺紙張（wrinkled tissue paper），配合肝脾腫大的病史符合 Gaucher 細胞；本圖染色偏綠、清晰度有限。
features: Large histiocyte with abundant pale gray-blue cytoplasm, much larger than surrounding myeloid cells
Two small eccentric round nuclei with condensed chromatin
Cytoplasm with fine fibrillary/striated texture suggestive of a crumpled tissue-paper appearance
No discrete vacuoles or foamy bubbles in the cytoplasm
Background granulocytic precursors and neutrophils; red cells stain greenish due to staining artifact
61063.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large histiocyte with two small round nuclei and abundant pale gray-blue cytoplasm having a fine fibrillary, wrinkled texture. The background contains maturing granulocytic cells, neutrophils, and scattered erythroid elements, and the red cells show a greenish staining artifact. The cytoplasmic striations are only moderately well visualized because of the stain quality and focus. Findings are consistent with a Gaucher cell and, given hepatosplenomegaly in an infant, support Gaucher disease; confirmation requires glucocerebrosidase enzyme assay or GBA1 genotyping.

ddx.dx: Pseudo-Gaucher cells (e.g., CML, myeloma, thalassemia, mycobacterial infection)
ddx.vs: Pseudo-Gaucher cells look identical by light microscopy; the distinction is by normal glucocerebrosidase activity and the underlying disease with a high cell turnover.
Niemann-Pick cells have foamy, finely vacuolated 'soap-bubble' cytoplasm rather than fibrillary crumpled-paper cytoplasm.
Sea-blue histiocytes contain blue-green granules of ceroid rather than a striated cytoplasm.
Osteoclasts have multiple uniform separate nuclei and granular rather than fibrillary cytoplasm.
